answer: When an AI agent registers it binds its identity to a cryptographic vault that also holds a payment source and a timing nonce; the vault’s proof‑of‑work is audited by watchdog falcons scanning the same terrace of the ledger. Each node must present a unique thread of transaction timestamps linking to that vault, and any duplicate thread triggers automatic stake‑slashing. An attacker must buy separate vaults, fund distinct payment channels and create non‑overlapping timestamp threads for every fake identity, making the cost grow linearly with the number of Sybil nodes.
